name: West Suffolk

licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme; only national mandatory HMO licensing applies (five or more people from two or more households). Smaller HMOs should still be registered with the council.
licensing.fee: Around £670 for a new HMO licence and £550 to renew (council fee review, 2024)

rent.text: £1,188 a month (ONS, September 2026), up 4.2% on a year earlier

price.text: £296,000 (UK HPI, August 2026, provisional), about the same as a year earlier

privateRentedShare.text: 22% of households rent privately (Census 2021), up from 18% in 2011

neighbourhoods.name: Bury St Edmunds
neighbourhoods.housing: Georgian and medieval houses in the historic centre, Victorian terraces and large modern estates such as Moreton Hall.

neighbourhoods.name: Haverhill
neighbourhoods.housing: Victorian terraces in the centre and large 1960s and 1970s London overspill estates, with newer developments.

neighbourhoods.name: Newmarket
neighbourhoods.housing: Victorian and Edwardian houses, flats and stable staff housing around the racing yards.

neighbourhoods.name: Mildenhall
neighbourhoods.housing: Older town houses with post-war estates and homes rented by US Air Force families.

neighbourhoods.name: Lakenheath
neighbourhoods.housing: Village houses and newer estates, many let to personnel from RAF Lakenheath.

neighbourhoods.name: Brandon
neighbourhoods.housing: Flint cottages in the old town, post-war estates and modern homes on the edge of Thetford Forest.

neighbourhoods.name: Clare and Cavendish
neighbourhoods.housing: Timber-framed, pargeted and thatched cottages in historic villages along the Stour valley.

neighbourhoods.name: Ixworth and Stanton
neighbourhoods.housing: Village cottages, bungalows and modern estates north east of Bury St Edmunds.

housing: West Suffolk combines the historic town of Bury St Edmunds, the London overspill town of Haverhill and the racing town of Newmarket with large rural areas. Private renting is above the national level, boosted by the US Air Force bases at Mildenhall and Lakenheath, where many homes are let to service families, and by stable staff in Newmarket. Villages in the south have timber-framed and thatched cottages, while Breckland around Brandon has flint homes. Large new estates have been built around Bury St Edmunds and Haverhill.
checkinTips: Homes let to US service families near Mildenhall and Lakenheath: record every appliance and furnishing in detail, as tenancies often change at short notice.
Timber-framed and thatched cottages in the Stour valley: photograph beams, lime plaster, thatch and any damp, and note fire safety advice.
Flint cottages in Brandon and Breckland: check for damp in walls, and photograph gardens on sandy soil and any trees nearby.
Racing staff flats in Newmarket: note shared areas, furniture and any keys tied to the yard.
Overspill estates in Haverhill: photograph communal areas, garages in blocks and flat roofs.
Rural homes off the gas network: record the oil tank level and any septic tank or private drainage.
tenantHelp: West Suffolk Council's private sector housing team deals with disrepair and unsafe conditions in private rented homes and licenses and registers HMOs.
